paragraphs.text: Of which he speaks 1Sa 23, when they did seek to betray him a second time.

The psalmist, complaining of his oppressors, prayeth forGod’s protection; and for the righteous punishment of his enemies, Psa 54:1-3. Placing his hope in God’s help, Psa 54:4,5, he promiseth a free sacrifice of thanksgiving to him, Psa 54:6,7.
i. e. by thy own strength, as the next words explain it, because I have no other refuge. Or, for thy name, i.e. for thy own glory, which is concerned in my deliverance.
i.e. judge or give sentence for me, or plead my cause, as this phrase is oft taken, as we have seen.

the Ziphites, whom, though Israelites, he calls strangers, in regard of their barbarous and perfidious disposition and carriage towards him, by which they showed themselves to be estranged from God, as the wicked are said to be, Psa 58:3, and from the commonwealth of Israel, and from all the laws of piety and humanity; for which causes he calls such persons heathens, Psa 59:5, and elsewhere.
they cast off all regard to thy presence and authority, and all fear of thy judgments.
paragraphs.anchor: They have not set God before them

paragraphs.text: consider it, and see the vanity of all your wicked practices against me.
he fights for them, and on my behalf, and therefore against all mine enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord is with them that uphold my soul

paragraphs.text: or, for or according to thy truth; whereby thou art engaged to fulfil thy promises made to me, and thy threatenings denounced against thine and mine implacable enemies.

not by constraint, as many do, because they are obliged to it, and cannot neglect it without shame and inconvenience to themselves; but with a willing and cheerful mind, which thou lovest in and above all sacrifices.
either thy name; or rather, to praise thy name;
i.e. an act of justice, and piety, and gratitude.
He speaks of it as a thing already done, either to express his assurance of it, or because this Psalm was made after it was done.
or, thy vengeance; which may be understood out of Psa 54:5. But there is no necessity of any supplement. The words in the Hebrew run thus,
either with delight, as this phrase signifies, Psa 22:17 27:4, and elsewhere; or without fear or shame. I shall not be afraid to look them in the face, having God on my side.
paragraphs.anchor: mine eye hath looked upon mine enemies
